class_name: 不必要-不必要-ナクテヨイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Lifts an obligation: the negative stem plus てもいい grants permission to skip an action (並ばなくてもいい). It also takes adjectives (高くなくてもいい) and the copula (学生でなくてもいい), where the siblings in this group are essentially restricted to verbs. ことはない and までもない instead argue that the action is pointless or excessive. Register runs from stiff なくともよい through neutral なくてもいい to casual なくたっていい.

examples.ruby: 切符[きっぷ]は車内[しゃない]でも買[か]えるから、並[なら]ばなくてもいいよ。
examples.english: You can buy a ticket on board, so there's no need to line up.

examples.ruby: 残[のこ]ったお皿[さら]は片付[かたづ]けなくたっていいからね。
examples.english: You can just leave the dishes that are left, okay?

examples.ruby: この資料[しりょう]は無理[むり]に覚[おぼ]えなくたっていい。
examples.english: You don't have to force yourself to memorize this handout.

patterns.usage_note: Attaches to the dictionary form and tells the listener there is no need for an action they are inclined to take, typically as reassurance or consolation (謝ることはない, 落ち込むことはない). には及ばない makes the same point as a courteous decline, and までもない calls the action excessive for an obvious matter. こたない is the spoken contraction; こともない is softer but also carries a separate sense, 'nothing so special as to …'.

examples.ruby: 一度[いちど]の失敗[しっぱい]でそんなに落[お]ち込[こ]むことはない。
examples.english: One slip-up is no reason to get that down on yourself.

examples.ruby: お土産[みやげ]なんて、わざわざ買[か]ってくることはないよ。
examples.english: You really don't need to go out of your way to bring back a souvenir.

examples.ruby: そんな噂[うわさ]をいちいち気[き]にするこたないよ。
examples.english: Don't waste your time letting gossip like that get to you.

glosses: there's no need to go so far as to …
patterns.usage_note: Attaches to the dictionary form and says the action would be excessive because the matter is obvious, trivial, or already settled: 言うまでもない, 地図を見るまでもない. ことはない tells someone there is no need for what they are inclined to do, and には及ばない courteously waves off a concern or an offer. It is more formal than なくてもいい and pairs with わざわざ and with verbs of stating or checking; the adverbial までもなく is common clause-initially.

examples.ruby: わざわざ本社[ほんしゃ]まで出向[でむ]くまでもない用件[ようけん]だ。
examples.english: It's a matter that hardly warrants a trip out to head office.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]通[かよ]っている道[みち]だから、地図[ちず]を見[み]るまでもない。
examples.english: It's a road I walk every day, so there's hardly any need for a map.

examples.ruby: この程度[ていど]の汚[よご]れなら、洗剤[せんざい]を使[つか]うまでもない。
examples.english: For a stain this minor, there's no need to break out the detergent.

glosses: no need to go to the trouble of …
patterns.usage_note: Attaches to the dictionary form and courteously declines a trouble, offer, or worry directed at the speaker (慌てるには及びません). ことはない makes the same point more bluntly, and までもない calls the action excessive for a self-evident matter. In real use it also takes bare nouns (お礼には及びません), which the corpus rule does not license. 及ばない separately means falling short of something (彼には及ばない), which is not this pattern.

examples.ruby: 予定[よてい]どおり進[すす]んでいますので、慌[あわ]てるには及[およ]びません。
examples.english: Everything is on schedule, so there's no cause for alarm.

examples.ruby: ご厚意[こうい]はありがたいのですが、そこまでしていただくには及[およ]びません。
examples.english: I appreciate the thought, but please don't go to that much trouble for me.

examples.ruby: たかが捻挫[ねんざ]ですから、入院[にゅういん]するには及[およ]びません。
examples.english: It's only a sprain, so there's no need for a hospital stay.

glosses: there would be no need to …
surely there is no call to …
it would hardly be necessary to …
patterns.usage_note: には及ばない with the literary negative conjecture まい, so the judgment is offered as inference: there would presumably be no need to do it (真に受けるには及ぶまい). It belongs to written narration and the weighty speech of fiction; conversation uses には及ばないだろう instead. Like its parent it attaches to the dictionary form, and まい has no past form.

examples.ruby: あの男[おとこ]の言葉[ことば]など、真[ま]に受[う]けるには及[およ]ぶまい。
examples.english: Surely there is no call to take a word that man says at face value.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]さら過去[かこ]を悔[く]やむには及[およ]ぶまい。
examples.english: There would be little point in regretting the past at this late hour.

examples.ruby: あんな些細[ささい]な手違[てちが]いで辞任[じにん]するには及[およ]ぶまい。
examples.english: A slip that trivial would hardly warrant resigning over.
